articles.title: Aluminium: Why Google’s Android for PC launch may be messy and controversial
articles.summary: Aluminium may not fully arrive till 2028 — and ChromeOS bows out in 2034.
articles.body: “Finally.” That was my first reaction when I heard Google would combine Android and ChromeOS into a single operating system. Android has long struggled on tablets, and ChromeOS always felt like too much of a stripped-down alternative to tempt me away from Windows and Mac. So last week, it was exciting to see a leaked first glimpse at Google’s Aluminium OS, and hear it may already be slated for an Intel Panther Lake laptop dubbed “Ruby” and a “Sapphire” high-end tablet. But the future may not be coming as fast as you’d think, and it might be messy when it gets here. According to previously unreported court documents in the Google search antitrust case, Aluminium won’t see a full release until 2028. Though Google’s head of Android, Sameer Samat, said last September that the combination of Android and Chrome is “something we’re super excited about for next year” — meaning 2026 — the documents suggest Aluminium won’t be ready to change the laptop world quite that soon. [Image: In a transcript obtained by The Verge from August 2025, Samat said that Google merely hopes to launch Aluminium in 2026 — “We’re working hard on it,” he said — and Google’s own lawyers seem less sure. In documents Google filed with the court, the new operating system’s “fastest path” to market involves offering it to “commercial trusted testers” in late 2026 before a full release in 2028. And while Chromebooks currently dominate in schools, the document suggests that “enterprise and education sectors” in particular will get Aluminium in 2028, not 2026. “Even when the new OS that runs Chromebooks becomes available, it will not be compatible with all existing Chromebook hardware, requiring Google to maintain existing ChromeOS at least through 2033 to meet its ‘10 year support commitment’ to existing users,” Google’s lawyers added. [Image: [Image: We already know ChromeOS won’t vanish from laptops right away. Google’s head of ChromeOS, John Maletis, confirmed as much to Chrome Unboxed earlier this month, adding that Google will honor its promise to give ChromeOS devices 10 years of automatic updates. But that means those devices may get those updates instead of an upgrade to Aluminium. Maletis told Chrome Unboxed: > In terms of devices being able to migrate over to the new stack, not all devices will be able to just because there are technical specifications…But a lot of the newer devices, we will be working on an ability for customers to migrate over. And here’s something that wasn’t previously reported: Google plans to kill off ChromeOS as soon as it can while meeting its 10-year support obligation for devices that won’t get Aluminium. The “timeline to phase out ChromeOS is 2034,” court documents reveal, adding that Google can’t do it any earlier because “jurisdictions have various rules for how long a device must be supported.” Why did Google lawyers admit all these things in court? At the time, those attorneys were trying to use these facts to argue that the US should not and cannot force Google to sell off Chrome after abusing its monopoly power over search. You can even see Google’s attorney leading the judge in that direction in one of my screenshots above: “So would divesting Chrome make it more difficult to support the ChromeOS software on the older computers?” Last September, in a controversial and widely reported decision, Judge Amit Mehta allowed Google to keep Chrome. What wasn’t so widely reported: Judge Mehta also agreed that he won’t ban Google from making self-preferencing deals with carriers and manufacturers to prioritize Google apps on their Aluminium OS devices. [Image: From the final judgment in US v. Google. The US v. Google remedies apparently don’t apply to Aluminium devices, even though Aluminium is largely Android. While Mehta’s final judgment bans deals that explicitly say things like “Motorola can’t put Google apps on their Android phones unless the phones default to Google Search” or “Apple can’t set their default AI app to ChatGPT if they want a share of Google search revenue on the iPhone,” Mehta has exempted ChromeOS and Aluminium from that ban. According to the final judgment, devices “on which the ChromeOS operating system or a successor to the ChromeOS operating system is installed” simply don’t count there. In a December 2025 opinion, the judge explained in part that’s because “Chrome is a necessary component of a ChromeOS device.” Perhaps that’s fair, and perhaps Chrome will be necessary for Aluminium as well. But perhaps it will only be necessary because Google designs it that way, giving the Chrome browser and Google apps special privileges that could possibly be delegated to other browsers and companies as well. [Image: Chrome and first-party Google apps are first-class citizens in Aluminium, while user apps are not. That could be important for a good user experience; it could be intentional lock-in; it could be neither or both. If Aluminium turns out to be largely Android for PCs, a version that just so happens to lock users into Google’s browser and Google’s app store and APIs, it might fly in the face of the world’s attempts to curb Google’s monopoly power. The tipster who pointed us to these documents wonders if, perhaps, Google may even be trying to shield Aluminium from repercussions in Epic Games v. Google, too — the case that may crack open the Google Play store to competition. While Judge James Donato’s original permanent injunction in Epic v. Google applies to Google’s dealings around the Play Store in general, presumably even if it’s installed on laptops, desktops, or any other kind of Android-based device, Google and Epic’s proposed settlement tweaks the injunction to only apply to smartphones and tablets that specifically run “the Android operating system.” That could exclude Aluminium as well as laptops and desktops in general, if approved. [Image: How would the court handle it if Google continued monopolistic behavior not on phones, but on Android-based Aluminium laptops? Google declined our request to fact-check the Project Aluminium timeline and other statements and documents from the court.

articles.title: Sony and Honda ain’t feelin’ the Afeela anymore
articles.summary: Sony and Honda’s joint venture are discontinuing the $90,000 Afeela sedan after Honda said it was overhauling its EV strategy.
articles.body: Sony and Honda have lost that lovin’ Afeela. The joint venture announced today that it would be discontinuing the $90,000 Afeela 1 electric sedan, as well as the unnamed Afeela SUV concept, as it adjusts to slower EV demand and policy pullbacks. In a statement, Sony Honda Mobility (SHM) determined there was not a “viable path forward” after Honda recalibrated its EV strategy following steep losses. Earlier this month, Honda said it would take a writedown of as much as 2.5 trillion yen ($15.7 billion) on its EV investments, representing the company’s first annual loss in over 70 years as a public entity. The automaker also put the kibosh on several planned EVs, including the Honda Zero Series Saloon and SUV. Now, the axe has fallen on the Afeela as well. “Since its establishment in September 2022, SHM has aimed to develop and sell high value-added mobility products and to provide mobility-related services by combining the technologies, expertise, and development capabilities of Sony and Honda,” the joint venture said in a statement. “However, as a result of Honda’s reassessment of its automobile electrification strategy announced on March 12, 2026, SHM will not be able to utilize certain technologies and assets that were originally planned to be provided by Honda at the time of SHM’s initial business planning. In light of this change, SHM has determined that it does not have a viable path forward to bring the Models to market as originally planned.” SHM said it would refund customers who deposited $200 to reserve a future Afeela. The Sony-Honda joint venture first revealed its Vision-S concept at CES in 2020. Since then, the companies have inched closer to production, but not close enough to offer test drives or anything beyond a hands-on with the high-powered infotainment system. Earlier this year, SHM started trial production of the Afeela 1 at Honda’s East Liberty Auto Plant in Ohio. And at CES in January, the joint venture introduced an SUV concept that it said would also go into production. In some respects, Afeela felt more like a platform for Sony’s entertainment offerings than a driving machine. It featured screens across the width of the dashboard, 40 sensors and cameras for semi-autonomous driving assistance, all-wheel drive, and hints at augmented reality integration and “virtual worlds” embedded into the driving experience. Sony recently said that Playstation 5 owners would be able to stream games directly on to the vehicle’s infotainment system. But now, the Afeela has become the latest victim of the auto industry’s EV retrenchment. Even with gas prices soaring and more customers becoming EV curious, automakers are paring back their model lineups and absorbing huge losses as a result. Some are scrambling to develop more affordable models to compete with an expected flood of cheap Chinese EVs, while others delaying the transition altogether. EV sales continue to climb in Europe and China, but automakers are facing challenges in those countries as well. It’s unclear what will become of Sony and Honda’s joint venture, which said it was continuing to hold discussions regarding its future plans. Honda, in particular, is in a tough spot, with declining US sales and an aging vehicle lineup. Last year, the company’s $60 billion plan to merge with Nissan fell apart amid disagreement about the future merged company’s structure.

articles.title: TCL is taking over Sony’s TV business
articles.summary: The new joint venture between TCL and Sony will begin operations next year producing TVs with TCL’s display tech and Sony’s Bravia branding.
articles.body: After signing a nonbinding agreement in January to spin off its TV business, today Sony officially announced that TCL will pay approximately 75.4 billion yen (over $473 million) for a 51 percent stake in a new joint venture called Bravia Inc., with Sony holding the remaining 49 percent. Bravia Inc., which will be headquartered in Sony’s Osaki office in Tokyo, is expected to begin operations in April 2027. When they announced the joint venture, the companies said the TVs it sells will have both Sony and Bravia branding, “while utilizing TCL’s advanced display technology, global scale advantages, industrial footprint, end-to-end cost efficiency, and vertical supply chain strength.” The new wholly owned subsidiary will assume Sony’s home entertainment business that covers the research and development, design, manufacturing, and support for various devices. These include Bravia televisions, other flat panel displays, projectors, home audio gear, and home theater systems. In today’s announcement, Sony senior vice president Kenji Tanaka says that through the strategic partnership, Bravia Inc. will “strive to provide new customer value to a global audience and achieve further growth in the home entertainment field.” As part of the deal, TCL will also purchase Sony EMCS (Malaysia) Sdn. Bhd., a subsidiary responsible for manufacturing Sony’s home entertainment products. Negotiations for another Sony manufacturing subsidiary, Shanghai Suoguang Visual Products Co., Ltd., are ongoing.

articles.title: Sennheiser Momentum 5 review: Great sound, incredible battery life, and few compromises | TechCrunch
articles.summary: I spent the last few weeks with the Sennheiser Momentum 5 to determine if this pair actually stands out, testing everything from sound quality and noise cancellation to comfort and battery life.
articles.body:
There are a lot of $300-$400 headphones on the market right now, and most of them blur together. I spent the last few weeks with the Sennheiser Momentum 5 to determine if this pair actually stands out, testing everything from sound quality and noise cancellation to comfort and battery life.

At $399.99, the Momentum 5 sit right in the middle of the premium headphone market. That puts them up against the pricier Sony WH-1000XM6 and Apple AirPods Max 2, while offering a more affordable option for anyone looking for high-end headphones.

Starting with sound, vocals sound natural and the bass is strong without taking over. The headphones allow you to start noticing little things in music, like a background harmony or a guitar string that cheaper headphones often tend to miss. If I had to describe the sound in one word, it’d be balanced.

The headphones support Dolby Atmos, which essentially means that music or movies sound like they’re coming from all around you instead of just left and right.

With this generation, Sennheiser doubled the microphone count to eight to improve the active noise cancellation (ANC). Voices and nearby chatter, which are usually the kind of sounds that can cut through weaker ANC, are noticeably quieter. Sennheiser claims this pair is up to three times more effective than the previous generation at blocking this type of noise.

Of course, it’s not quite at the level of blocking out everything like a plane’s engine, but it does the job effectively without making your ears feel weirdly pressurized as can be the case with some ANC headphones.

As for comfort, the headphones aren’t as premium-feeling as Apple or Sony headphones that I’ve tried in the past, but given that the Momentum 5 cost less than its competitors, it’s a trade-off that’s hard to complain about.

The battery life is genuinely impressive. It’s rated for up to 57 hours, and that figure held up in my testing. For context, that’s roughly twice the battery life of the Sony WH-1000XM6 and nearly three times that of the AirPods Max 2.

And when the battery does run out, a 10-minute charge gets you up to seven hours of playback, while a full charge takes about two hours.

A notable difference that the Momentum 5 offers that its competitors don’t is a user-replaceable cell, which means you can swap out the battery once it degrades instead of having to buy a whole new pair.

What I wasn’t expecting, but found surprisingly useful, was how thin the carrying case is. I’ve never really been able to fit a pair of headphones into my medium-sized purses, but the Momentum 5 fit perfectly. It’s also a big plus when traveling, since the case doesn’t take up much space in your luggage.

With the headphones’ companion app, Smart Control Plus, you can adjust a bunch of different settings. There’s an 8-band EQ that lets you tune the sound yourself or choose from one of Sennheiser’s presets. The app also lets you adjust the level of ANC rather than just switching it on or off, and there’s an anti-wind mode you can access there too. The “Sound Personalization” feature walks you through a listening test and creates a sound profile tailored to your hearing preferences.

The app gives you a decent amount of control over the Momentum 5, and I found it pretty easy to navigate as most of the settings are quite straightforward.

Overall, the Sennheiser Momentum 5 is a solid option at this price. They offer great sound, the battery life is excellent, and the downsides are pretty minor. They’re heavier than the Sony WH-1000XM6, and aren’t as comfortable as some Sony or Apple options, but at $399.99, they’re cheaper than both while still delivering where it matters.

articles.title: Bigg Boss Telugu 10: No elimination this week as Mukesh sacrifices captaincy and immunity
articles.summary: The latest episode of Bigg Boss Telugu 10 came with a major twist as there was no elimination this week after captain Mukesh decided to give up his
articles.body: The latest episode of Bigg Boss Telugu 10 came with a major twist as there was no elimination this week after captain Mukesh decided to give up his captaincy and immunity to save Varshini and Vamsi. Both contestants were in the danger zone, and Nagarjuna gave Mukesh the final decision. He gave him a chance to cancel the elimination on the condition that he accept the consequences that came with the decision.At the end of the elimination process, Varshini and Vamsi were still in the danger zone. Nagarjuna then turned to Mukesh and said, “Captain Mukesh, this is your final temptation. The decision is yours. You can save the contestant who is about to be eliminated.” He added, “You will lose your captaincy. Along with that, you will also lose the immunity that came with it. You will be directly nominated. If you agree to all three conditions, the elimination will be cancelled.”The offer surprised Mukesh, who simply could not believe what he was hearing. Varshini and Vamsi both stood waiting for his response. He pondered the request before finally saying, “I feel that both of them are potential contestants, and I’m ready to give up my captaincy if both of them are saved.”Nagarjuna then announced that there would be no elimination this week as a result of Mukesh’s decision. This came as a relief to Varshini and Vamsi, who were moments away from seeing one of them leave the house.As far as Mukesh was concerned, his decision came at a steep price. According to the rules set by Bigg Boss, he would have to forfeit both his captaincy and immunity and be directly nominated. Nagarjuna later announced that Apoorva would take over as captain and receive the immunity power. She earned the opportunity because she and Mukesh had both emerged as winners in the captaincy task earlier in the week.Mukesh’s decision has already become one of the biggest talking points of the season. Although Varshini and Vamsi have both been saved, his gamble could very well come back to haunt him. After all, he has sacrificed his captaincy and is now facing direct nomination. It will be interesting to see what happens next week.Get the latest TV News, TV Shows and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Want to score well': Friend says Sahil Wakode told her in 'last call' he was caught cheating
articles.summary: Mumbai crime branch records friend’s statement in IIT Bombay student Sahil Wakode suicide probe; she says he admitted cheating in a last call after exam.
articles.body: MUMBAI: The Mumbai crime branch probing the abetment to suicide of IIT-Bombay student Sahil Wakode has recorded the statement of a friend, who told investigators that she was the last person to speak to him on the phone.According to police, Wakode told her during the call that his thermodynamics theory paper had gone poorly and that he was worried as he had wanted to score well. He also told her that he had been caught cheating during the exam, they said.The friend, who is among at least six students whose statements have been recorded so far, told police that Wakode appeared stressed during their conversation. However, investigators have so far not found any clear indication of stress or distress in the material examined during the probe.Wakode (22), a second-year BTech student, was found dead in his hostel room hours after the exam on Sept 18.Investigators are reconstructing his movements after he left the exam hall. CCTV footage has established that Wakode left the hall after he was asked to do so and returned later.The CCTV footage has been sent for forensic analysis. Investigators are also examining Wakode’s locked iPhone, hoping to retrieve his last calls, messages and other data. Experts have so far been unable to access the phone because of its password.Police said they are currently recording the statements of students and other witnesses and will subsequently record the statement of Prof Suryanarayana Doolla, who was present during the exam.Wakode’s parents made an emotional appeal to IIT-B students to continue their protest and sought preservation of any evidence relating to the death. In another video message addressed to students, Wakode’s father said on Sunday he had been unable to enter the campus despite visiting it two or three times. He reiterated that he planned to begin a hunger strike at Azad Maidan from Monday, demanding access to the institute and justice for his son.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: WhatsApp may soon bring redesigned navigation bar for Android users: Report
articles.summary: Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp is reportedly working on a refreshed design for its Android app.
articles.body: Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp is reportedly working on a refreshed design for its Android app. According to a latest leak by WaBetaInfo, WhatsApp is testing a new bottom navigation bar separate from the main interface with rounded corners and a floating layout. “The floating bar and rounded edges are the main similarities with the iOS version. However, this does not mean that WhatsApp will also add the same translucent effect to the bottom navigation bar on Android,” the report adds.As per the report, the redesigned navigation bar was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.38.10 update, which is available through the Google Play Store. It is currently under development and has not enabled it for beta testers either.Cybersecurity company warns of WhatsApp scam 'spreading fast'In another news, Quick Heal Technologies Limited recently issued a warning on an ongoing WhatsApp-based malware campaign targeting finance teams, senior executives, chartered accountants and individual business users. According to the cybersecurity firm, the campaign spreads through compromised WhatsApp accounts and is evolving rapidly, with attackers adopting new file formats and evasion methods to bypass security controls and establish persistent access to victims’ devices.In its warning, the company cited an investigation conducted by its researchers at Seqrite Labs. The study shows that the campaign relies on trust rather than unsolicited messages from unknown numbers. Once a WhatsApp account is compromised, attackers use it to forward malicious files to the account holder’s existing contacts. Because the messages appear to come from a known colleague, client, friend or business associate, recipients may be more likely to open the attachment without independently verifying it.As per the study, the attackers are using finance- and compliance-themed filenames to create urgency and familiarity. Malicious attachments have been disguised as routine business documents, including “Financial Report,” “Account Statement,” “Outstanding Payment List” and “Debt Confirmation.” Some variants also impersonate urgent communications from regulatory institutions, including the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in an effort to pressure recipients into opening the files immediately.You use AI every day. articles.title: Honor’s Magic 9 Pro Max has a big camera and a bigger battery
articles.summary: New photography partner Arri is making its presence felt in Honor’s Magic 9 Pro Max already.
articles.body: Honor launches its new Magic 9 flagship phones in China today, and the 9 Pro Max features a design revamp, a capable camera, and a colossal battery. This is Honor’s first flagship launch — Robot Phone aside — since it announced its collaboration with camera company Arri. The initial impact is twofold. The new camera island is Arri-inspired, drawing from the “three-lens turret” design first introduced in 1937’s Arriflex 35, complete with a knurled texture around the main lens. [Image: Arri used variants of this three-lens turret design across most of its film cameras. Arri has played a part in the camera itself, contributing the ability to shoot in Arri LogC3, together with 14 preset Arri Look LUTs, access to Arri’s wider library of official and third-party LUTs, and support for the APV 10-bit 4:2:2 codec. The cameras themselves include a 200-megapixel main lens using a 1/1.28-inch-type sensor, a 3.5x telephoto using the same resolution and a 1/1.4-inch sensor, and a 50-megapixel ultrawide — though this latter lens doesn’t support all the Arri Cinema Mode features. A “cinema-grade” directional microphone should help with video recording too. Less technically impressive, but just as useful, will be the square-format selfie camera, which like Apple’s Center Stage will be able to capture in either landscape or portrait. Honor says that the wider camera island is more space-efficient, leaving extra space for a huge 8,800mAh battery, now up to 40 percent silicon content. The 9 Pro Max is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. I asked Honor why it picked the Extreme version, given the 9 Pro Max doesn’t support the 8K60 or 4K240 video recording that chip enables, and was told it was “about delivering a complete and consistent flagship experience, rather than pursuing a single benchmark result.” [Image: The Magic 9 Pro Max supports Honor’s G200 and G500 teleconverter lenses, plus a custom SmallRig video kit. The Magic 9 series launches in China today. Honor has confirmed that an international launch is coming, but we’re still waiting to find out when.

articles.title: DANA PERINO: The untold story of the remarkable people who make Fox News possible
articles.summary: Anchor Dana Perino marks Fox News Channel's 30 years with a tribute to the behind-the-scenes producers, crews and teams who power every breaking news moment.
articles.body: FOX NEWS ALERT! You’re joining our coverage live as Fox News Channel celebrates 30 years of on-air excellence. Thirty years? It went by so fast. And yet, a 30th anniversary doesn’t happen by accident. Fox News makes it look easy. It’s not. The work behind the scenes is incredible to witness. FOX NEWS TOUTED AT ANNUAL UPFRONT PRESENTATION TO ADVERTISERS: ‘WE’RE NOT JUST COMPETING, WE ARE DOMINATING’ Let’s take a moment to recognize the people our viewers never see — the ones who make it possible for the shows to get on the air and for those of us in front of the camera to have complete confidence that the product reaching our viewers is informative and entertaining. Having that confidence matters to the anchors, hosts and guests. It’s critical to know the research is solid, the technology is working, the pictures are right, and, if something changes in an instant, that the team has your back. Nearly the entire building is organized around making that possible. FOX NEWS DIGITAL THUMPS ALL NEWS BRANDS INCLUDING BROADCAST NETWORKS IN KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS DURING JULY Aside from the hours I’m on air, I walk into work so happy. I love my routine — and knowing that the plan could change in an instant. It keeps me on my toes. My day begins with a security guard who likes to announce, "Talent is in the building!" precisely because he knows the word "talent" makes me cringe. I blush, walk faster, and we laugh about it every single morning. I often see one of the custodial staff on my way up to my office, and one joins me in trying to get a tradition going of saying, "Morning morning!" every day. We have a streak — we never miss. Long before I arrive, the producers have already been working. They get up hours before we do, thinking about what would make a good show — not simply what we are going to say, but what the audience is going to experience. They’re looking for the best and latest video that captures an event, making graphics to help explain the story (I love charts!) and writing scripts that grab the viewer and keep them watching. And then, at a moment’s notice, they may have to tear up the entire rundown when breaking news changes everything. Suddenly, the carefully planned show is gone, and the team is shifting to something happening across the country or around the world. They have to gather information, verify it, find the right pictures, reach the right correspondents and guests, and help us understand what matters — fast. That kind of flexibility only looks effortless when the people doing it are exceptionally good at their jobs. My day begins with a security guard who likes to announce, ‘Talent is in the building!’ precisely because he knows the word 'talent' makes me cringe. I blush, walk faster, and we laugh about it every single morning. I remember once interviewing an Afghan man who witnessed the Abbey Gate airport bombing in August 2021, when President Joe Biden pulled our troops out. This man picked up an injured child, carried her to safety and then came on air with us. He was a man with no hope. And while I am usually very stoic on air, I was about to cry. WOUNDED MARINES RELIVE THE HARROWING KABUL AIRPORT ATTACK IN EXPLOSIVE NEW FOX NATION DOCUMENTARY I will never forget the reassuring voice in my ear from the line producer: "You’re OK. You’re OK." My tears dried up. The interview continued. Assistants are a lifeline for us — they produce our lives. They do the research, keep the schedule, block and tackle, and get in front of problems. The scope and scale of their talents are immense, and without them, we’d be lost. Our technology teams keep us connected to breaking news and events around the world in real time — something we all take for granted right up until the second something doesn’t work. And then, of course, there are those who help us look our best. The wardrobe department has a great eye and is always there with a pin or a piece of tape when we need it. The hair and makeup team is by far the best in the business. Name another? You can’t. FOX NEWS LEADS ALL NEWS BRANDS IN YOUTUBE VIDEO VIEWS AND SOCIAL ENGAGEMENT FOR SECOND QUARTER 2026 They’re also our confidants — I’ve worked with the same team for almost 15 years, and they’ve become my sister-friends. Sure, they make sure I’m camera-ready at an hour when most reasonable people are still in pajamas, but they also know when I’ve had a tough night, could use some encouragement, need to laugh and when it’s better just to let me sit quietly for a few minutes. I can’t wait to see them every day and catch up. So many others to mention — the directors who know how to get the best reaction shots, the cameramen who never miss an angle, and the lighting technicians we wish we could take with us everywhere. And there’s a special relationship with a stage manager who can communicate an entire paragraph with one glance. There are also those who laugh at our jokes — it’s very gratifying to hear those chuckles. On the road, another kind of magic happens. Our crews can take a barn, a convention hall, a parking lot or almost anywhere else and turn it into a beautiful television set. Hollywood should be so lucky to know these people. And amid the enormous logistical challenge of covering an election or a breaking-news event, someone still remembers the little things: Dana likes warm water in her cup. Dana would love a yoga mat in her room if we’re going to be here for a very long time. Dana needs a footstool (always!). Those things may sound small, but they make all the difference. They say: We know you. We’ve got you. Go do your job. That same support extends far beyond the studio. Our media relations team promotes our work, tells our stories and, when we need it, defends us vigorously. They are in the arena with us and knowing they are there matters. The same is true of our radio, podcast and digital teams, which have evolved right alongside the technology and opened up more and more ways for us to reach people. What once lived mostly on a television screen now lives in earbuds, phones, websites and across platforms that did not even exist when Fox News began. The technology changes, but the mission remains the same: Find the audience and serve them well. And there are so many others whose names never appear on the screen. You don’t just work alongside people — you live a lot of life alongside them. These are not just colleagues. After enough years, they become deep friendships, and all the while, I have laughed so much. FOX NEWS DIGITAL HITS 165 MILLION UNIQUE VISITORS IN MAY TO CRUSH BROADCAST NETWORKS, NEWS COMPETITORS I have also leaned on this group for comfort during some of life’s hardest moments, including when my dad passed away earlier this year. And I have had the privilege of sharing in the joy, too — marriages, babies and now, after all these years, even grandbabies. That is what longevity really looks like. You don’t just work alongside people — you live a lot of life alongside them. We have celebrated, mourned, adapted and endured more than a few difficult seasons. And I think we are stronger because of it. I’ve been at Fox for nearly 17 years, and somehow I still feel new compared with the OGs who built this network and made it what it is today. But excellence still comes down to people and our corporate culture. Without their singular focus on getting it right, we would not be number one, and we would not have lasted 30 years. Because of them — along with the vision and leadership from the top, including our founders — I have tremendous confidence in the years ahead. articles.title: MARTHA MACCALLUM: After 22 years, here's why I'm grateful to call Fox home
articles.summary: From the 2004 Democratic convention floor to the beaches of Normandy, two decades of reporting shaped a career.
articles.body: Twenty-two years ago, I made the best move of my career. My early years were spent at The Wall Street Journal and CNBC. But coming here changed my life in so many positive ways that I can’t imagine what any other path would have looked like. I am deeply grateful that I trusted the gut feeling that told me I belonged here. On my first day, Jeff Hark, who was overseeing the scheduling of reporters and anchors, asked me about my family. He knew I had three young children, and he wanted to assure me that Fox understood the pressures of young professionals raising kids. Defensive at first, I insisted I could handle it and wouldn’t be bothering him with requests for time off, but then I realized he actually meant it. It was such a smart company perspective that it made me want to work even harder, knowing they would have my back. Fox liberated me to grow and take on so many new challenges. The environment was still scrappy, and the growth was exponential. Every opportunity I leaned into opened a door. That first year, I asked to be part of the election team covering the November 2004 presidential race. I offered to stand on a street corner in Boston and report on how the DNC was affecting traffic. Kidding, but not kidding — I just wanted to be in the "room where it was happening"! I soon found myself reporting from the floor of the Democratic convention alongside correspondents Carl Cameron and Major Garrett, two of our most seasoned political reporters. I was exuberant and terrified. But I survived, and it was the beginning of 20 years of covering elections for Fox News. I have traveled the world, covered presidents and kings, and perhaps most rewarding of all, I have had the honor of walking the beaches of Normandy with our war heroes and sharing their stories, from Berlin, Korea, Vietnam and Afghanistan. At Fox, a deep respect for our veterans was encouraged in a way that would not have happened anywhere else. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION I am forever grateful for our Fox family here. For Lachlan, Suzanne and Jay, and everyone else who feels like home. We are bonded by a love for our country. We are driven to hold it to the highest standard. To hold those who govern it accountable. And to pray for its continued success. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Happy 30th birthday, Fox. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FROM MARTHA MACCALLUM

articles.title: Googlebook OS will be available for some Chromebooks.
articles.summary:
Googlebooks will be available at retailers later this week, but you might not need to buy a new device to get Google’s latest laptop OS. “Many of our newest Chromebook devices will be eligible to transition over to Googlebook OS,” says Google in a support note targeted at Chromebook enterprise and education customers. Google hasn’t shared migration paths or device eligibility yet, but it’s encouraging to see the search giant sticking to what it announced earlier this year.

articles.title: Sony quits CES.
articles.summary:
Sony’s keynotes were once a highlight of the annual Consumer Electronics Show in Las Vegas. But the company’s presence has shrunk in proportion to its slow exit from consumer electronics. And with Bravia now a TCL brand, and the Afeela EV joint venture with Honda scrubbed, there’s little reason to attend.

articles.title: Uber removed its branding from its safari vehicles after “outrage” from local tour guides.
articles.summary:
According to the Wall Street Journal, local guides were initially concerned Uber would be sending regular drivers out for its tours of Kenya’s Nairobi National Park, rather than licensed guides:
> “It got to a point where safety was paramount,” said Uber East Africa General Manager Imran Manji, who helped create the service. He imagined a worst-case scenario where Uber-branded vehicles could be targeted in retaliation. “We don’t want to put the driver or the guide in danger, and we don’t want the passengers in any danger,” he said.
